appraisal_events.evidence: « tu peux continuer, lui dit-elle ironiquement, en esquissant le geste de quelqu'un qui vous fait la barbe »; « Regarde, il souffre », lui dit-elle tout bas, «dans l'élan momentané d'une cruauté sadique».
appraisal_events.explanation: Rachel mockingly mimes a barber's gesture at Saint-Loup and then, in what the narrator explicitly calls a sadistic impulse, points out his visible suffering to the dancer she is admiring, humiliating him in front of a rival.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup is shown visibly suffering, mocked, and exposed by Rachel in front of the dancer he cannot compete with, leaving him locally humiliated.
The narrator directly labels her impulse 'cruauté sadique,' casting Rachel negatively in this local moment even though the deeper affection is not in question.

ambiguities: Rachel is never named in this excerpt itself (referred to only as 'elle'/'lui'); her identity is inferred from the reference sheet and the well-known Saint-Loup jealousy scene rather than from an explicit surface form in the passage.

The narrator explicitly calls Rachel's act 'cruauté sadique' but immediately qualifies that it was 'nullement en rapport avec ses vrais sentiments d'affection pour Saint-Loup,' softening what would otherwise be a stronger, more stable negative characterization of her.
